# DISK references

Generate the four NPY files under `testdata/cv/features/disk` (from
[#1368](https://github.com/opencv/opencv_extra/pull/1368)) using ONNX Runtime
CPU and OpenCV preprocessing. Requires `numpy`, `opencv-python` (or an OpenCV
Python build), and `onnxruntime`. Match the ONNX Runtime version to the C++
build.

## Resize and engine selection

Current OpenCV `5.x` DISK uses `blobFromImage` with `INTER_LINEAR`. Use the
script's default `--resize linear` for that branch. `--resize linear-exact`
changes the input pixels and is **only** for a build that enables
`strictResize` in DISK. The OpenCV version string does not identify which
preprocessing a build uses. Do not use exact resize with a build that lacks
that flag.

Tags, their net sizes and their keypoint counts are all derived at run time,
not hardcoded: tags come from whichever `box_in_scene_*_kpts.npy` files are
committed, a `WxH`-shaped tag supplies its own net size, the `default` tag's
net size is read out of `disk.cpp`'s `kDefaultDiskInputSize`, and each tag's
keypoint count `n` is the row count of its own committed file. `--opencv-src`
points at the sibling `opencv` checkout used for that last lookup; override it
if your checkout isn't a sibling of `opencv_extra`.

Inference in this script uses ORT CPU. The C++ tests default to `ENGINE_OPENCV`,
which can produce different feature ordering and numerical results. To validate
ORT references with the C++ ORT engine, build OpenCV with `WITH_ONNXRUNTIME=ON`
and set `OPENCV_FORCE_DNN_ENGINE=2`. The script never changes the test engine;
leave the variable unset to check the default OpenCV engine.

## Commands

From `testdata/dnn`:

```sh
python download_models.py disk

# Regenerate for current 5.x, without replacing the checked-in references.
python generate_disk_references.py --output-dir /tmp/disk-linear

# Check both tags' files AND run both C++ regressions against those files.
python generate_disk_references.py --output-dir /tmp/disk-linear --check \
    --test-binary /path/to/opencv-build/bin/opencv_test_features

# Reproduce references for a build with strictResize enabled in DISK.
python generate_disk_references.py --resize linear-exact --output-dir /tmp/disk-exact
python generate_disk_references.py --resize linear-exact --output-dir /tmp/disk-exact \
    --check --test-binary /path/to/strict-resize-build/bin/opencv_test_features

# Python/NPY comparison only; this cannot establish C++ compatibility.
python generate_disk_references.py --check-npy
```

Inputs are the downloaded model and `testdata/cv/shared/box_in_scene.png`. Use
`--testdata` and `--models-dir` to override input locations. Omit `--output-dir`
to replace the four files in `testdata/cv/features/disk`. Regenerate all four
together.

`--check` requires `--test-binary`, writes no reference files, and exits 1 on
NPY mismatch or C++ failure. It stages a temporary testdata tree so both C++
tests read the selected image, model, and `--output-dir` references.
`Features2d_DISK.regression_default` and `Features2d_DISK.regression_512x384`
must both actually run and pass; skipped or missing tests fail validation.

`--check-npy` compares Python-generated arrays only, after sorting both sides
into the same canonical (x, y) position order — DISK's top-N selection uses an
unstable `partial_sort`, so a raw row-by-row diff reports spurious mismatches
even when the same keypoints were picked. Keypoint tolerance is `1e-4`,
descriptor tolerance `1e-5`. It prints explicitly that C++ tests were not run.

## ORT does not reach ENGINE_OPENCV parity for DISK

Unlike ALIKED/LightGlue, this script's `--check` does not pass against a real
build, on either `--resize linear` (against the already-committed references)
or `--resize linear-exact`. The `default` tag's mismatch is consistent with the
resize fix (positions match, scores and descriptors shift outside tolerance).
The `512x384` tag, however, also fails by a similar amount in both modes, even
though its net size equals the source image size, so `blobFromImage` never
resizes there at all — `strictResize` is a no-op for that tag. That rules out
the resize patch as the cause for `512x384`.

DISK's regression tolerance (`1e-4` absolute on scores of magnitude ~70-90) is
tight enough that it requires the reference to come from the same engine build
that runs the test, not just an equivalent one. Neither ONNX Runtime nor a
separately installed `opencv-python` wheel (a different build from whatever
produced the committed references) reaches that bar; both differ from a local
`opencv_test_features` by amounts similar to what's shown below. Use this
script to validate preprocessing logic and to sanity-check a candidate change,
not to produce the values that actually get committed.

## Generating the committed references: dump_disk_references.cpp

The committed `.npy` files are generated by `dump_disk_references.cpp`, a
small standalone tool in this same directory that calls `DISK::create()` and
`detectAndCompute()` directly and links against the OpenCV build under test.
Because it runs inside that exact build, its output matches
`opencv_test_features` by construction — there is no cross-engine gap to
account for.

```sh
# Build against an existing OpenCV build tree (adjust include/lib paths to
# match your layout; OPENCV_BUILD is a CMake build directory for `opencv`
# with the features and dnn modules enabled).
g++ -std=c++17 -O2 \
  -I "$OPENCV_BUILD" \
  -I "$OPENCV_SRC/modules/core/include" \
  -I "$OPENCV_SRC/modules/imgproc/include" \
  -I "$OPENCV_SRC/modules/imgcodecs/include" \
  -I "$OPENCV_SRC/modules/dnn/include" \
  -I "$OPENCV_SRC/modules/flann/include" \
  -I "$OPENCV_SRC/modules/geometry/include" \
  -I "$OPENCV_SRC/modules/features/include" \
  dump_disk_references.cpp \
  -L "$OPENCV_BUILD/lib" -Wl,-rpath,"$OPENCV_BUILD/lib" \
  -lopencv_features -lopencv_dnn -lopencv_imgcodecs -lopencv_imgproc \
  -lopencv_geometry -lopencv_flann -lopencv_core \
  -o dump_disk_references

# Dump both tags, reading n from the currently committed files.
./dump_disk_references "$TESTDATA/dnn/disk.onnx" "$TESTDATA" /tmp/disk-dump

# Validate before committing: run against a staged copy of the dump output.
# generate_disk_references.py's check_cpp() staging layout applies the same
# way here (cv/shared, cv/features/disk -> dump output, dnn/disk.onnx).
```

`dump_disk_references <disk.onnx> <testdata_root> <output_dir> [tag ...]`
reads each tag's keypoint count `n` from `testdata_root/cv/features/disk/
box_in_scene_<tag>_kpts.npy` (so it preserves whatever count is already
committed, the same contract `generate_disk_references.py` follows), runs
`DISK::create(modelPath, n, 0.0f, imageSize)` with `imageSize` parsed from the
tag (`Size()` for `"default"`, `WxH` otherwise), and writes `_kpts.npy`
(x, y, score) and `_desc.npy` in the same layout as the Python script. With no
tags given, it dumps `default` and `512x384`.

## Validation

Tested against a local `5.x` build at `0f9fc7031d` (includes the strictResize
patch for DISK), IPP-accelerated, via
`opencv_test_features --gtest_filter=Features2d_DISK.*`:

| Reference source | `regression_default` | `regression_512x384` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Committed (generated opencv_extra#1368, 2026-06) | FAIL (max score diff 0.00021) | FAIL (max score diff 0.00035) |
| `generate_disk_references.py --resize linear-exact` (ORT) | FAIL (max score diff 0.993) | FAIL (max score diff 0.00035) |
| `dump_disk_references.cpp` against this build | **PASS** | **PASS** |

The committed `512x384` reference was already stale before the strictResize
patch, for reasons unrelated to it (general drift between the June build that
produced it
and later `5.x` history) — `dump_disk_references.cpp` corrects both tags.
